description: Run ONE SQL statement against a registered foreign Postgres connection (by connection_name) and write its result rows to a TSV; the transaction commits after the file is written, so a data-modifying CTE takes effect. What the statement may do is decided only by the registered role's own server-side GRANTs. Returns immediately with a job_id and status 'queued' (D0.3 deferred-completion shape) — the dispatch returning is NOT the same as the job finishing. When the job completes, the result is ALWAYS written to the caller-supplied output_tsv_path, never returned inline, at any size. This connection targets an arbitrary customer database, so there is no vendor-imposed row ceiling to defer to; the limit below is entirely our own policy. Defaults to 500 rows to avoid exhausting the target database and disk, and to discourage pulling all rows for client-side filtering that a WHERE clause should do instead. To fetch more, pass acknowledge_default_limit_override=true together with an explicit row_limit (up to 1000) — both are required together, and a row_limit above 1000 is refused rather than silently clamped. For pulls beyond 1000 rows, use export_query instead (same override mechanism, hard cap 50000). Use list_connections to discover registered names. When the goal is validating that records exist or picking one to act on next, prefer selecting stable ID columns over email addresses or other PII-bearing fields — the query decides what columns come back, so a narrower SELECT is both cheaper and lower-exposure.
embedding_description: Run a quick, ad-hoc SELECT or other single statement against a registered external Postgres database for everyday spot-checks, landing the answer in a small workspace TSV -- never inline. Dispatches asynchronously, returning a job_id while the small TSV is written in the background, usually fast. Defaults to 500 rows. Prefer stable ID columns over PII fields.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Dispatch envelope: job_id (string) and status ('queued'). This is NOT the query result — the TSV handle (path, columns, row_count, truncated) arrives separately when the job completes and is delivered as its own message.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: This call only confirms the job was queued — do not present job_id/status as the query result. Acknowledge the request is in flight; the TSV handle lands in a follow-up message when the job completes. Once delivered, confirm the write: the path, the row_count, and the column list. The file may contain potentially sensitive corporate database content (data_sensitivity 0.5) -- name the path for downstream use (open it, feed it to create_spreadsheet_from_files, join it with other exports) but never inline its contents into context. If truncated is true, say so and point to export_query or an acknowledged row_limit override for the rest.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Run one SQL statement against a registered foreign Postgres connection and write its rows to a TSV and write the result to a workspace TSV file.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: external_pg.invalid_params: missing connection_name/sql/output_tsv_path, the path's parent directory does not exist, acknowledge_default_limit_override and row_limit were not given together, or row_limit exceeded the 1000 hard cap. external_pg.export_path_refused: the path must be absolute, have the required suffix where specified, and lie under a saved path address, the session folder or solet home, outside the installation tree. Input files must already exist. external_pg.connection_unknown: no connection registered under that name. external_pg.read_only_sql_transaction: the SERVER refused a write because the transaction is read-only there (a hot standby, or the role's default_transaction_read_only setting). external_pg.query_failed: a SQL syntax or missing-object error in your query. external_pg.auth_failed / external_pg.permission_denied: the registered credential was rejected. external_pg.timeout: the query exceeded the statement timeout. external_pg.platform_db_refused: the connection targets the platform's own database (refused).
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: external_pg.invalid_params naming the override pair: pass BOTH acknowledge_default_limit_override=true and an explicit row_limit, or neither (for the 500-row default); a row_limit above 1000 must go through export_query instead. external_pg.invalid_params with a missing-parent message: create the parent directory first. external_pg.export_path_refused: ask "where will you save this?" and use the returned folder, or say "save exports for <project> in <folder>" to save a project location. Keep it outside the installation tree; input files must already exist. external_pg.connection_unknown: run list_connections to see registered names. external_pg.read_only_sql_transaction: point the write at a primary server or a role whose default_transaction_read_only is off. external_pg.query_failed: fix the SQL. external_pg.timeout: narrow the query or add a LIMIT. external_pg.auth_failed/permission_denied: ask the operator to re-check the registered connection.
